## Introduction & background

A Low-Dropout (LDO) regulator is fundamentally an analog feedback loop. An op-amp (the error amplifier) compares a stable reference voltage (provided by a Zener diode or bandgap reference) against a scaled-down fraction of the output voltage. If the output sags due to an increased load, the op-amp increases the drive to a pass transistor to let more current flow. The "dropout" voltage is determined by the minimum physical voltage drop required across the pass transistor for it to remain conductive.

## Core equations

Output Voltage (Non-inverting configuration):
$$V_{out} = V_{Zener} \left(1 + \frac{R_1}{R_2}\right)$$

Dropout Voltage Limit:
$$V_{in,min} = V_{out} + V_{CE(sat)}$$

## What you're building

1. A discrete LDO voltage regulator circuit on a breadboard stepping 9 V down to 3.3 V.
2. A load-regulation testing setup swapping out output resistors to measure voltage sag when pulling 10 mA versus 100 mA.
3. A dropout testing procedure to slowly lower the 9 V input supply until the 3.3 V output can no longer maintain regulation.

## Activity

Breadboard it: LM358 error amp + PNP/PMOS pass element + 5.1 V Zener reference + feedback divider, 9 V in → 3.3 V out. Step the load 10 mA → 100 mA (swap resistors); record Vout each step (= load regulation). Reduce Vin until Vout sags (= dropout).
